cohort: The study included 145 term infants born to mothers diagnosed with pre-gestational diabetes (type I or type II).
finding: There was no significant increase in peak neonatal transcutaneous bilirubin in term infants of mothers with pre-gestational diabetes after undergoing thirty-seconds of delayed cord clamping, and no significant differences were found in secondary outcomes.
cross-section timing: The study period was from October 2014 to August 2017, comparing outcomes of infants born before and after a 30-second delayed cord clamping protocol was implemented in January 2016.
